summary.en: Benjamin Alire Sáenz, an acclaimed writer, poet, and novelist, has passed away at the age of 71. Known for his works for young adults, he explored themes related to his sexuality and experiences living on the US southern border, becoming the first Latino recipient of the PEN/Faulkner award.

body.en: Celebrated writer, poet and novelist for young adults drew upon his sexuality and life on US southern border Benjamin Alire Sáenz, an award-winning fiction writer and poet who drew upon his sexuality and his life on the southern border, has died at age 71. He was the first Latino to win the PEN/Faulkner prize. Sáenz, who produced a story collection that won the PEN/Faulkner prize and a young adult novel that received acclaim from readers and reviewers and condemnation from censors, died on 28 July in El Paso, Texas, after a lengthy illness, according to a spokesperson for Simon & Schuster. His legacy, shaped by his unique experiences and literary contributions, now stands as a testament to a life fully lived. In every life, there is a time for all things, and ultimately, a time to return to Yahweh.
reflection.zh: 本杰明·阿里尔·萨恩斯的逝世提醒我们，世上的生命都有其注定的终点。他以独特的经历和文学贡献塑造的遗产，如今成为他充实一生的见证。在每个生命中，万事皆有时，最终，我们都要归回雅伟。

title.en: EU calls for stronger borders after Ceuta migrant crossings
title.zh: 欧盟呼吁在休达移民过境后加强边境

summary.en: Ursula von der Leyen has called for action ahead of an urgent EU interior ministers meeting to discuss the issue.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及领导、智慧与公共责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen has called for "united action" on border security after the chaotic influx of tens of thousands of migrants from Morocco into the Spanish exclave of Ceuta last week.

Spain ⁠estimates that about 69,500 migrants ​have now returned to Morocco, exceeding initial estimates of 50,000. The official death toll on the Spanish side of the border stands at 72, with 11 deaths on the Moroccan side.

On Tuesday, EU interior ministers will have emergency talks by video conference to discuss the issue.

The scenes in Ceuta have strained relations among some of the EU's 27 member states.

In a letter to Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez, von der Leyen praised his "swift handling" of the crisis.

But she added: "From this incident, it is clear that we must do more to further strengthen our borders at critical points."

In response to the Ceuta crossings, Italy temporarily suspended the Schengen arrangement with Spain.

The Schengen agreement eliminates border checks and now encompasses more than 450 million people and 29 countries in Europe.

Finland and Denmark backed Italy's move, while Czech Prime Minister Andrej Babiš urged a temporary suspension of Spain's Schengen membership.

In response, Sánchez said he had "serious concerns" about some European governments and pointed out that Ceuta was not part of the Schengen area.

While most had shown "support and solidarity", he said other European governments had chosen to attack Spain, "driven by prejudice, fake news, ignorance, or political interest".

In her letter to the Spanish PM, von der Leyen warned that "the protection of all our external borders is a shared European responsibility", while calling for "vigilant monitoring and the use of physical barriers where needed".

Tuesday's video conference will be a chance to draw "lessons" from the Ceuta episode, von der Leyen said, warning the challenges of illegal immigration require "a common European response, united action and solidarity".

She urged the EU to "double down" in five areas: preventing irregular migration in the first place via cooperation with partner states; strengthening external borders; implementing early warning systems; dismantling smuggling networks and reinforcing returns.

Sánchez has accused migrant traffickers of exploiting a decision recently made by the country's supreme court which constrained the government's right to immediately deport people who had arrived by sea.

The country's Interior Minister, Fernando Grande-Marlaska, said on Saturday that the situation had almost returned to normal and the country was working on inflatable barrier to prevent illegal migration via the water.
body.zh: 上周数万名摩洛哥移民混乱地涌入西班牙飞地休达后，欧盟委员会主席乌苏拉·冯德莱恩呼吁就边境安全采取“联合行动”。 西班牙估计约有 69,500 名移民​现已返回摩洛哥，超过最初估计的 50,000 人。边境西班牙一侧的官方死亡人数为 72 人，摩洛哥一侧有 11 人死亡。 周二，欧盟内政部长将通过视频会议举行紧急会谈，讨论这一问题。 休达事件导致欧盟 27 个成员国中一些国家之间的关系变得紧张。 冯德莱恩在给西班牙首相佩德罗·桑切斯的信中赞扬他对危机的“迅速处理”。 但她补充道：“从这起事件中可以明显看出，我们必须采取更多措施，在关键时刻进一步加强我们的边境。” 为了应对休达过境点，意大利暂时中止了与西班牙的申根安排。 申根协议取消了边境检查，目前涵盖欧洲 29 个国家和超过 4.5 亿人口。 芬兰和丹麦支持意大利的举动，而捷克总理安德烈·巴比什则敦促暂时取消西班牙的申根会员资格。 桑切斯回应称，他对一些欧洲政府“严重关切”，并指出休达不属于申根区。 他表示，虽然大多数国家都表现出了“支持和声援”，但其他欧洲国家政府“出于偏见、假新闻、无知或政治利益”，选择攻击西班牙。 冯德莱恩在给西班牙首相的信中警告说，“保护我们所有的外部边界是欧洲的共同责任”，同时呼吁“保持警惕并在需要时使用物理屏障”。 冯德莱恩表示，周二的视频会议将是从休达事件中汲取“教训”的一个机会，他警告说，非法移民的挑战需要“欧洲共同应对、联合行动和团结”。 她敦促欧盟在五个领域“加倍努力”：首先通过与伙伴国合作防止非正常移民；加强外部边界；实施预警系统；摧毁走私网络并加强回返。 桑切斯指责移民贩运者利用该国最高法院最近做出的一项决定，该决定限制了政府立即驱逐通过海路抵达的人的权利。 该国内政部长费尔南多·格兰德-马拉斯卡周六表示，情况已基本恢复正常，该国正在研究充气屏障，以防止通过水上非法移民。

title.en: The endurance gambit: Could Iran's pressure strategy force Trump to give in?

summary.en: Iran doesn't want a decisive military victory, experts say. Its real plan is more complex than the US may have expected.

body.en:
Iran is betting it can outlast Washington by turning the Middle East's trade routes, shipping lanes and energy infrastructure into pressure points that steadily raise the cost of confrontation, according to Gulf officials and analysts.

Rather than seeking a decisive military victory, Iran is pursuing a strategy of calibrated escalation aimed at widening the conflict without triggering full-scale war.

The goal, they say, is to convince the United States and its allies that containing the crisis is more costly than accommodating Iran's demands over the Strait of Hormuz .

The message from Iran is that unless the US accepts a new status quo that gives Iran a greater role in Hormuz, the conflict could spread beyond the Gulf.

By putting multiple maritime chokepoints and energy assets at risk, Iran believes it can strengthen its hand in any future negotiations.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

"Iran, from the beginning, has tried to out-escalate the United States by stretching out its escalation options so that it always has something new to bring every week — a new geography, a new type of weapon, a new type of target," Michael Knights of the Washington Institute told the Reuters news agency.

"The bigger advantage they have is not that they can hurt America or Israel," Knights added. "Their big advantage is that they can hurt the regional states and the global economy."

Having demonstrated its ability to disrupt traffic through Hormuz, through which about a fifth of global oil consumption flowed before the war, Iran has signalled that no maritime chokepoint is off limits.

Threats to the Red Sea and Saudi energy infrastructure suggest a broader effort to raise the cost of protecting global commerce while testing the US' tolerance for disruption.

Iran's approach reflects what one Gulf source described as a belief among Revolutionary Guards commanders that "they can get more".

They see an opportunity in what they regard as President Donald Trump's reluctance to become deeply entangled in another Middle East conflict ahead of November's midterm elections .

"The Iranians ... believe that by widening the war and increasing the pressure, he will eventually give in," the Gulf source said. "Trump thinks he can hit the Iranians hard and bring them to the negotiating table, but they won't bend."

Trump said talks with Iran would take place on Monday after earlier saying he had called off an imminent attack in hopes of securing a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Iran, however, said it was not currently holding talks with the United States.

title.en: US reports first two deaths linked to 'explosive diarrhoea' outbreak
title.zh: 美国报告首批两例死亡病例与“爆炸性腹泻”爆发有关

summary.en: The illness caused by parasitic infection that spreads through contaminated food or water is not generally life-threatening, health officials say.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及真理、分辨与诚实。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Michigan health officials have confirmed the first two deaths linked to the ongoing cyclospora outbreak, a parasitic infection spread through contaminated food or water that can cause severe diarrhoea.

The two individuals had "significant underlying health conditions that may have been impacted by cyclosporiasis and dehydration", state health authorities said.

The foodborne illness has spread to 45 states, with nearly 7,000 laboratory-confirmed cases reported nationwide, according to the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC).

While the outbreak has infected thousands of people, the CDC says deaths from cyclosporiasis are far from common, as it is "not usually life-threatening".

Michigan's health department did not provide further details about those who have died.

The state is at the epicentre of the current outbreak and its records show more than 11,000 cases and 193 hospitalisations, although many have not been laboratory-confirmed.

The heat-loving parasite infects the intestines and is transmitted through faecal contamination.

Past outbreaks have occurred when people consumed fruits or vegetables irrigated with water contaminated by faeces.

The CDC recommends washing all produce under running water, including those that are labelled as pre-washed.

But washing alone might not be enough to rid produce of the parasite. Cooking produce to a temperature of at least 70°C (158 °F) can kill the parasite, the agency recommends.

Officials have linked this year's widespread outbreak to lettuce imported from Taylor Farms in Mexico, a key supplier for many food establishments in the US.

US fast-food chain Taco Bell said it has removed lettuce from the supplier from its menu. Taylor Farms itself announced a voluntary recall of lettuce sourced from central Mexico.

UK health officials too have warned about the outbreak following recent cases contracted by returning travellers.
body.zh: 密歇根州卫生官员已确认前两例死亡与正在发生的环孢子虫爆发有关，这是一种通过受污染的食物或水传播的寄生虫感染，可导致严重腹泻。 州卫生当局表示，这两人“存在严重的潜在健康状况，可能受到环孢子虫病和脱水的影响”。 据美国疾病控制与预防中心 (CDC) 称，食源性疾病已蔓延至 45 个州，全国报告了近 7,000 例实验室确诊病例。 尽管这次疫情已经感染了数千人，但疾病预防控制中心表示，环孢子虫病造成的死亡并不常见，因为它“通常不会危及生命”。 密歇根州卫生部门没有提供有关死者的更多详细信息。 该州处于当前疫情爆发的中心，其记录显示有超过 11,000 例病例和 193 例住院治疗，尽管许多病例尚未得到实验室确认。 这种嗜热寄生虫会感染肠道，并通过粪便污染传播。 过去爆发疫情的原因是人们食用了用被粪便污染的水灌溉的水果或蔬菜。 疾病预防控制中心建议用流水清洗所有产品，包括那些标记为预洗的产品。 但仅清洗可能不足以消除农产品中的寄生虫。该机构建议，将农产品烹饪到至少 70°C（158°F）的温度可以杀死寄生虫。 官员们将今年的大范围疫情与从墨西哥泰勒农场进口的生菜联系起来，该农场是美国许多食品企业的主要供应商。 美国快餐连锁店塔可钟表示，已将供应商的生菜从其菜单中删除。泰勒农场本身宣布自愿召回来自墨西哥中部的生菜。 在最近出现回国旅行者感染病例后，英国卫生官员也对疫情爆发发出了警告。

reflection.en: This story draws attention to truth, discernment, and honest speech. Philippians 4:8 reminds us to meet sharp headlines with discernment and truthful speech, asking how faithful people can respond with wisdom instead of noise.
reflection.zh: 这则新闻让人想到真理、分辨与诚实。Philippians 4:8提醒我们，在快速变化的新闻里，仍要以分辨与诚实表达来回应，并学习用祷告与分辨代替情绪化判断。

verse.textEn: Whatever is true, whatever is noble, whatever is right, whatever is pure, whatever is lovely, whatever is admirable — think about such things.
verse.textZh: 凡是真实的、可敬的、公义的、清洁的、可爱的、有美名的，这些事你们都要思念。

title.en: Iran says it is in talks with Oman but not the US after Trump says negotiations to resume
title.zh: 特朗普建议周一与伊朗重启谈判

summary.en: President Trump has proposed new talks with Iran to begin on Monday, though Tehran has not yet responded to the suggestion. This comes after previous claims by Trump that a negotiated end to the conflict was near, only for military strikes to resume.
summary.zh: 特朗普总统提议周一与伊朗重启谈判，但德黑兰尚未对此建议作出回应。此前，特朗普曾表示冲突的谈判解决已近在咫尺，但随后军事打击又重新开始。

body.en:
Iran says it is negotiating with Oman to reach "an understanding" over a temporary route through the Strait of Hormuz to allow commercial shipping to resume.

The statement came after US President Donald Trump said new talks on ending the war in Iran would begin on Monday - and that he had called off "massive" strikes on the country for this purpose.

Trump did not specify who would take part in the talks. Iran, however, said it was not negotiating with the US - and had no plans to do so.

Tehran's denial appears to have irked the US president, who later wrote on his Truth Social media platform that Iran's leadership was "unbelievably duplicitous".

Speaking to reporters at the White House later, he insisted talks were in fact taking place.

"They're going on right now... this is the last chance for them to sign a good document," he said.

At the weekend, Trump had said the "perimeters" of a deal had been agreed - and would include reopening Hormuz, the vital waterway whose closure by Iran has sent oil prices soaring.

Tehran has repeatedly closed off the strait since the US and Israel started attacks on the country in February.

Speaking on board Air Force One on Sunday, he said Iran "knew the extent" of the planned US strikes "because they saw it forming".

Trump declined to outline a deadline for a deal to be struck with Tehran, adding: "We'll just see how it is. We're ready to go anytime we want... I'm not looking to kill people."

Trump added that Saudi Arabia's Crown Prince Mohammed Bin Salman - as well as US partners such as the United Arab Emirates and Qatar - had urged him against conducting strikes over the weekend.

"We were all set to go," Trump said. "The reason they asked is [that] they think there's a deal," he said. "There's a deal on Hormuz, and there will be a deal on the nuclear."

Global oil prices fell on Monday morning in Asia trading after Trump's announcement. Brent Crude oil was down by 4.5% at $83.98 (£62.26), while US-traded oil was 4.6% lower at $80.74 (£59.85).

Energy prices have fluctuated since the conflict started on 28 February as traders reacted to disruptions to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.

Around 20% of the world's crude oil and liquefied natural gas (LNG) usually flows through the strait.

Vessel-tracking data from trade intelligence company Kpler suggests commercial shipping through the strait has slowed - with 51 vessel crossings between 30 July and 2 August. This is a drop of around 28% compared to the previous 4 days, in which 71 crossings were recorded through the strait.

Talks to end the conflict - mostly facilitated by mediators - collapsed last month, ending a ceasefire agreed in April.

title.en: Russia says seven killed and 40 injured by Ukrainian drone hitting busy beach
title.zh: 俄罗斯称乌克兰无人机袭击繁忙海滩致七人死亡四十人受伤

summary.en: Officials say at least seven people were killed and 40 injured, including three children, when a Ukrainian drone crashed at a popular resort on Russia's Black Sea coast.
summary.zh: 俄罗斯官员称，一架乌克兰无人机坠毁在黑海沿岸一处热门度假海滩，造成至少七人死亡，四十人受伤，其中包括三名儿童。

body.en:
A drone hit a busy beach in southern Russia, killing seven people including three children, local authorities have said.

In social media footage verified by the BBC, a drone can be seen hurtling towards a cliffside before crashing into a fireball on the beach below as tourists look on from the shore and in the water.

The total number of injured reached 40, with 17 people hospitalised, said the governor of the Krasnodar region Veniamin Kondratyev.

He accused Ukraine of "a deliberate strike on civilians". Ukraine has not commented. Both sides deny targeting civilians deliberately.

It is unclear what the drone was targeting. Some Ukrainian Telegram channels have claimed it crashed onto the beach as a result of electronic warfare which jammed the drone's signal. Several eyewitnesses were quoted by Russian media as saying gunfire preceded the explosion, indicating that air defences may have tried to shoot the drone down.

The crash occurred on a beach near the village of Arkhipo-Osipovka on the Black Sea. With its warm climate, long beaches and developed tourist infrastructure it is a popular holiday destination for Russians, in particular since sanctions have curtailed international travel for many.

Tourists and residents of Arkhipo-Osipovka told local media outlets that no sirens sounded ahead of the drone attack.

"We covered ourselves with sun loungers, and didn't see where it exploded," said one holidaymaker. Another person said that while they did not see the drone hit they could hear "gunfire, like a machine gun" followed by an explosion.

"This all happened in front of my children. My child is having a nervous breakdown," said a third.

Over the course of the last year Ukraine has had increasing success in carrying out long-range strikes deep into Russia, hitting energy infrastructure and commercial warehouses it says are used for military purposes.

On several occasions these strikes have caused civilian deaths, with eight people in different Russian cities killed at the weekend.

Russia meanwhile has launched attacks on residential areas and cities from the start of its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, killing and injuring thousands of civilians.

On Saturday, at least nine people were killed and dozens injured in Russian ballistic missile strikes on Kyiv, according to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky. The city's mayor said a residential building in the Shevchenkivskyi district was partially destroyed, trapping people inside. Last week a strike on a building in Ukraine's Kryvyi Rih area killed a family of 10.

In recent weeks Ukrainian strikes have in particular targeted warehouses belonging to Wildberries – a large online retailer dubbed the "Russian Amazon".

body.zh: 地方当局表示，一架无人机袭击了俄罗斯南部一个繁忙的海滩，造成七人死亡，其中包括三名儿童。 在英国广播公司(BBC)核实的社交媒体视频中，可以看到一架无人机飞向悬崖边，然后撞上下面海滩上的火球，游客们从岸边和水中观看。 克拉斯诺达尔地区州长韦尼亚明·康德拉季耶夫 (Veniamin Kondratyev) 表示，受伤总人数达到 40 人，其中 17 人住院。 他指责乌克兰“蓄意袭击平民”。乌克兰尚未发表评论。双方均否认故意针对平民。 目前尚不清楚无人机的目标是什么。一些乌克兰电报频道声称，由于电子战干扰了无人机的信号，飞机坠毁在海滩上。俄罗斯媒体援引几名目击者的话称，爆炸前发生了枪声，表明防空系统可能试图击落这架无人机。 坠机事故发生在黑海阿尔希波-奥西波夫卡村附近的海滩上。凭借其温暖的气候、绵长的海滩和发达的旅游基础设施，它成为俄罗斯人受欢迎的度假胜地，特别是因为制裁限制了许多人的国际旅行。 阿尔希波-奥西波夫卡的游客和居民告诉当地媒体，无人机袭击前没有响起警报。 一位度假者说：“我们用躺椅盖住自己，但没有看到爆炸的地方。”另一个人说，虽然他们没有看到无人机被击中，但他们可以听到“枪声，就像机枪一样”，然后发生爆炸。 “这一切都发生在我的孩子们面前。我的孩子精神崩溃了，”第三个人说。 去年，乌克兰在深入俄罗斯的远程打击方面取得了越来越大的成功，袭击了据称用于军事目的的能源基础设施和商业仓库。 这些袭击多次造成平民死亡，周末俄罗斯不同城市有八人死亡。 与此同时，俄罗斯从 2022 年 2 月全面入侵乌克兰开始，就对居民区和城市发动袭击，造成数千名平民死伤。 乌克兰总统泽连斯基表示，周六，俄罗斯弹道导弹袭击基辅，造成至少九人死亡、数十人受伤。该市市长表示，舍甫琴基夫斯基区的一栋住宅楼部分被毁，有人被困在里面。上周，乌克兰克里沃罗格地区一栋建筑遭到袭击，造成一家十口死亡。 最近几周，乌克兰的罢工特别针对 Wildberry 的仓库，该公司是一家被称为“俄罗斯亚马逊”的大型在线零售商。 最近的一次罢工袭击了弗拉基米尔地区的一个仓库，...

title.en: Dry Danube River threatens nuclear power in Romania, Hungary
title.zh: 多瑙河干涸威胁罗马尼亚和匈牙利核电站

summary.en: Low water levels in the Danube River are impacting nuclear power generation in Hungary and Romania. Hungary's Paks plant is operating at reduced capacity, while Romania's military has intervened to improve water flow to the Cernavoda plant.
summary.zh: 多瑙河水位下降正在影响匈牙利和罗马尼亚的核电生产。匈牙利的帕克斯核电站目前以约10%的容量运行，而罗马尼亚军方已采取措施，炸毁岩石以改善切尔纳沃德核电站的水流。

body.zh: 由于缺乏冷却河水，匈牙利帕克斯核电站的运行能力约为 10%。在罗马尼亚，军方炸毁了一块岩石露头，以改善切尔纳沃达核电站的水流量。 由于天气持续炎热干燥，多瑙河和其他水道水位创历史新低，一些中欧和东欧国家正面临电力短缺和对工业的影响。 匈牙利勉强避免了关闭其唯一的核电站，但仍将其发电量降至一小部分。在罗马尼亚，海军拆除了多瑙河河床上裸露的岩石露头，试图改善水流。 在塞尔维亚，水力发电量受到干旱的严重影响。 预计本周天气将持续炎热干燥，但几乎没有缓解的迹象。 罗马尼亚军方引爆了多瑙河支流上因水位低而暴露的岩石露头，试图改善切尔纳沃达核电站的冷却水流量，该核电站通常供应该国约五分之一的电力。 士兵们在上游约 50 公里（约 30 英里）处引爆了一块岩石。这些碎片将被带到一个战略地点并沉入水中以帮助提高水位。 国防部长拉杜·米鲁塔 (Radu Miruta) 表示，此次行动取得了成功，并表示军方数十年来一直在等待进入并拆除岩石的机会。 米鲁塔说，如果部分水转移失败，该工厂可能不得不在周四之前完全关闭。 看守总理伊利·博洛扬 (Ilie Bolojan) 表示，在与能源密集型行业代表召开危机会议后，汽车制造商达西亚 (Dacia) 和福特 (Ford) 已同意暂停在罗马尼亚的生产直至 8 月 19 日。他表示其他公司也会采取类似的措施。 匈牙利总理彼得·马扎尔表示，上周最初宣布的帕克斯核电站周一全面关闭的情况是有可能避免的。 但这个拥有四个反应堆的发电站通常产生匈牙利近一半的电力生产和约三分之一的电力消耗，但周一的运行能力略高于 10%。 匈牙利已要求工业用户抑制消费，并要求家庭自愿储蓄。周一，电动货运列车也被停运，以减少电网负荷。 “我们已经进入关键时期。由于自我克制，网络稳定，目前消耗量远低于计划水平。最后一台 Paks 涡轮机已投入运行。我很快就会从（电网运营商）MAVIR 控制室报告。”他说。 马扎尔周一早些时候还表示，“未来的水资源管理预测......

Yahweh placed humanity in the garden to “work it and keep it,” a responsibility that extends to managing our resources and infrastructure wisely in a changing world. This news underscores our deep dependence on the natural systems Yahweh...

title.en: Rhine falls to record low levels as drought strains Europe's rivers
title.zh: 莱茵河水位降至历史新低，干旱使欧洲河流承压

summary.en: Low water levels in the Rhine, Danube, and Po rivers have disrupted the transport of goods and reduced electricity generation across Europe.
summary.zh: 莱茵河、多瑙河和波河的低水位已导致货物运输受阻，并减少了欧洲的电力产出。

body.en:
The River Rhine has fallen to record low levels in several locations in Germany and the Netherlands as prolonged heatwaves continue across Europe.

Last week, levels were measured in Cologne in western Germany and in Lobith, where the Rhine crosses from Germany into the Netherlands, that were lower than at any point since records began.

Other major European rivers with important transport, industrial and agricultural functions have also seen record low levels, including the Danube, which flows through 10 countries, and Italy's Po river.

Drought conditions remained stable and critical in most of Europe and worsened in central-western Europe in mid-July, according to the EU's Drought Observatories.

Renewed heatwave conditions are due to continue for at least another week, pushing temperatures above 40C in many central and southern European countries.

Germany's Low Water Information System (NIWIS) said that 44% of the Rhine measuring stations and 78% of those on the Danube had recorded extremely low water levels at the end of July.

The Rhine - which starts in the Swiss Alps and empties in the North Sea - is one of Europe's busiest waterways. Decreasing water levels have sparked concerns about the economic fallout of having to limit navigation and shipping.

On Friday, the navigable water depth at the chokepoint of Kaub near Koblenz hit the 2018 record low of 25cm, before recovering slightly on Monday.

The Kaub gauging station in western Germany is a key indicator of navigability on the Rhine because it measures how heavily cargo vessels can be loaded. Low water levels measured there can severely restrict inland shipping.

Martin Wolters of the Rhine Waterways and Shipping Authority told German outlet WDR that although shipping on the Rhine was unlikely to be suspended altogether, precautions would have to be taken, such as spreading out cargo among more vessels to make them less heavy.

In time, this can result in higher transport costs and supply bottlenecks, Wolters said.

"There comes a time when loads are too small to be worthwhile or vessel owners are worried about damaging their ships," one commodity trader told Reuters.

Last week, the waters of the Danube fell to the lowest levels for 30 years in several countries, including Serbia and Romania, leaving Hungary's only nuclear power plant on the brink of shutting down.

The facility is operating at a reduced capacity and officials are monitoring whether it may need to be taken offline completely.

The drought of the Danube is also causing serious disruption to power supplies in Serbia and Romania.

Serbia cut output at its coal-fired power plants due to the lack of water disrupting cooling systems, while Romania carried out a controlled explosion on a large rock on the banks of the Danube...
body.zh: 随着整个欧洲持续长时间的热浪，德国和荷兰的几个地方莱茵河水位已降至历史最低水平。 上周，德国西部科隆和莱茵河从德国流入荷兰的洛比斯测得的水位水平低于有记录以来的任何时候。 其他具有重要运输、工业和农业功能的欧洲主要河流也出现了创纪录的低水位，包括流经10个国家的多瑙河和意大利的波河。 据欧盟干旱观测站称，7 月中旬，欧洲大部分地区的干旱状况依然稳定且严峻，但中西欧地区的干旱状况更加恶化。 新一轮的热浪天气预计将持续至少一周，导致许多中欧和南欧国家的气温超过 40 摄氏度。 德国低水位信息系统（NIWIS）表示，7月底莱茵河上44%的测量站和多瑙河上78%的测量站记录到极低水位。 莱茵河发源于瑞士阿尔卑斯山，注入北海，是欧洲最繁忙的水道之一。水位下降引发了人们对必须限制航行和航运造成的经济影响的担忧。 周五，科布伦茨附近考布阻塞点的通航水深触及2018年历史最低点25厘米，周一略有回升。 德国西部的考布测量站是莱茵河适航性的关键指标，因为它测量货船的装载重量。那里测得的低水位会严重限制内陆航运。 莱茵河航道和航运管理局的马丁·沃尔特斯 (Martin Wolters) 告诉德国媒体 WDR，尽管莱茵河航运不太可能完全暂停，但必须采取预防措施，例如将货物分散到更多船只上，以减轻其重量。 沃尔特斯说，随着时间的推移，这可能会导致运输成本上升和供应瓶颈。 一位大宗商品贸易商告诉路透社：“总有一天，装载量太小而不值得，或者船东担心损坏他们的船只。” 上周，包括塞尔维亚和罗马尼亚在内的多个国家多瑙河水位跌至30年来的最低水位，导致匈牙利唯一的核电站处于关闭边缘。 该设施的运营能力正在降低，官员们正在监测是否需要完全关闭该设施。 多瑙河的干旱还导致塞尔维亚和罗马尼亚的电力供应严重中断。 由于缺水破坏了冷却系统，塞尔维亚削减了燃煤发电厂的产量，而罗马尼亚则对多瑙河畔的一块大岩石进行了受控爆炸……

reflection.en: The low water levels in Europe's major rivers remind us of creation's vulnerability and its deep connection to human well-being. As the Apostle Paul observed, the natural world often groans under strain, impacting our daily lives and economies. This news calls us to reflect on our relationship with the earth and the broader implications of its suffering.
reflection.zh: 欧洲主要河流的低水位提醒我们，受造界是脆弱的，它与人类的福祉息息相关。正如使徒保罗所言，自然界常在重压下叹息，影响着我们的日常生活和经济。这则新闻呼吁我们反思与地球的关系，以及受造界受苦的深远影响。

verse.textEn: We know that the whole creation has been groaning as in the pains of childbirth right up to the present time.
verse.textZh: 我们知道，一切受造之物一同叹息、劳苦，直到如今。

title.en: Ceuta: EU calls borders a 'shared European responsibility'
title.zh: 休达：欧盟称边境是“共同的欧洲责任”

summary.en: The European Commission has offered Morocco increased assistance for border security at Ceuta and Melilla, advocating for a unified approach from the EU member states. Interior ministers are scheduled to discuss this matter on Tuesday.

title.en: Can PM Modi reconnect with India's Gen Z?
title.zh: 莫迪总理能否与印度 Z 世代重新建立联系？

summary.en: Student protests exposed a growing disconnect between PM Narendra Modi's BJP and young Indians. Experts say Instagram reels alone won't close it.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Student protests exposed a growing disconnect between PM Narendra Modi's BJP and young Indians. Experts say Instagram reels alone won't close it.

As students filled India's streets to demand accountability from the government , Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi seemed to have realized that he needed to connect more effectively with the country's youth.

Modi posted on Instagram a rare selfie video in which he said he was pained by their suffering and promised remedial steps. But it was not enough to satisfy the protesters' concerns, and five Gen Z-style reels later, that gap seems as wide as ever.

"We ain't friends," one comment under the first reel read. It echoed thousands of others reacting to a midnight video drop from the PM. 

In one of Modi's lesser-produced videos, he addressed the youth as "friends" before finally speaking about the exam at the center of the protests.

It was the prime minister’s response to the biggest political crisis he has faced in his third term so far, over a cancelled high-stakes medical entrance exam which affected millions of aspirants.

Since the first video, he's improved camera angles and lighting, tried varied backgrounds, and even started and ended the videos himself like a one-man content creator. The response remains tepid.

For Modi's ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), the protests came at the peak of its power, but the unrest has dimmed that shine, and the disconnect with the youth is substantial, experts told DW.

In 2024, the average age of MPs elected to India's Parliament reached a record 56 years, which is a problem, said Shipra Baduni, CEO of Young Leaders for Active Citizenship, because there is not much youth representation in the legislature. 

India has traditionally had vibrant youth participation at the university level, where student parties have long been affiliated with national and regional parties. 

"Student politics has not only given a pulse check, or given a platform for young people to be able to express frustration, or anger, or dissent," said Baduni. "It's also given some of these parties and leaders today."

"We've seen systematically over the last one decade that it has been cut down," she added. "There is a very evident push to say that students should only study, and there is no need for students to engage in politics."

"Where is the space for a young person to express their frustration? If you go on social media to criticize the government, there is a crackdown. Offices are screening your social media."

But Baduni believes the responsibility to connect with the youth doesn't lie with the central government alone: "It's the job of my ward councillor or my local elected leader to come out and say, 'let me talk to the young people in my locality,...
body.zh: 学生抗议暴露了纳伦德拉·莫迪总理领导的印度人民党与印度年轻人之间日益严重的脱节。专家表示，仅凭 Instagram 卷轴并不能关闭它。 当学生们涌上印度街头要求政府问责时，印度总理纳伦德拉·莫迪似乎意识到他需要与该国的年轻人建立更有效的联系。 莫迪在 Instagram 上发布了一段罕见的自拍照视频，他在视频中表示，他对他们的痛苦感到痛苦，并承诺采取补救措施。但这还不足以满足抗议者的担忧，在五次 Z 世代风格的卷轴之后，这种差距似乎和以前一样大。 “我们不是朋友，”第一卷下的一条评论写道。这与数千人对总理午夜发布的视频的反应相呼应。 在莫迪制作较少的一段视频中，他将年轻人称为“朋友”，然后最后谈到了抗议活动中心的考试。 这是总理对他第三个任期迄今为止所面临的最大政治危机的回应，这场危机是因为高风险的医学入学考试被取消，影响了数百万有抱负的人。 自第一个视频以来，他改进了摄像机角度和灯光，尝试了不同的背景，甚至像一个单独的内容创作者一样自己开始和结束视频。反应依然不温不火。 专家告诉德国之声，对于莫迪领导的执政党印度人民党（BJP）来说，抗议活动正值其权力的顶峰，但骚乱已经削弱了它的光芒，而且与年轻人的脱节也很大。 积极公民青年领袖首席执行官希普拉·巴杜尼 (Shipra Baduni) 表示，2024 年，当选印度议会议员的平均年龄达到创纪录的 56 岁，这是一个问题，因为立法机构中的青年代表并不多。 印度传统上在大学层面上有充满活力的青年参与，学生政党长期以来一直隶属于国家和地区政党。 巴杜尼说：“学生政治不仅为年轻人提供了一个表达沮丧、愤怒或异议的平台。” “今天也给了其中一些政党和领导人。” “在过去的十年里，我们已经系统地看到它已经被削减，”她补充道。 “有一种非常明显的推动力，即学生应该只学习，没有必要让学生参与政治。” “年轻人表达不满的空间在哪里？如果你在社交媒体上批评政府，就会遭到镇压。有关部门正在审查你的社交媒体。” 但巴杜尼认为，与年轻人建立联系的责任不仅仅在于中央政府：“我的选区议员或当地民选领导人的工作就是站出来说，‘让我与当地的年轻人交谈，......

reflection.en: This story draws attention to justice, dignity, and accountability. Micah 6:8 reminds us to meet sharp headlines with justice tempered by mercy, asking how faithful people can respond with wisdom instead of noise.
reflection.zh: 这则新闻让人想到公义、尊严与问责。Micah 6:8提醒我们，在快速变化的新闻里，仍要以带着怜悯的公义来回应，并学习用祷告与分辨代替情绪化判断。

title.en: Russia: Bridge-building with North Korea
title.zh: 俄罗斯：与朝鲜架起桥梁

summary.en: In the far east, well away from world events, Russia and North Korea are building their first road connection. The project has set alarm bells ringing in Ukraine.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
In the far east, well away from world events, Russia and North Korea are building their first road connection. The project has set alarm bells ringing in Ukraine.

For years, Khasan was little more than a very remote place on the edge of Russia . Less than 500 people live in the village in the country's far east, more than 5,600 miles (9,012 kilometers) from Moscow. But it's here that Russia shares a mere 10.5-mile border with North Korea — and Khasan is the only Russian settlement along that short stretch. Since 1959, the so-called Korean-Russian Friendship Railway Bridge has crossed the Tumen River here, serving as the only land connection between the two countries.

But in recent years, Russia and North Korea have been building a parallel road bridge just a few hundred yards away. The bridge is now nearing completion ahead of schedule, raising concerns in Kyiv that Russia could use it to secretly bring North Korean troops to the front lines in Ukraine .

Since the start of Russia's invasion of Ukraine in 2022, Moscow and Pyongyang have improved their ties . Both countries face Western sanctions and are diplomatically largely isolated. In June 2024, Russian President Vladimir Putin and North Korean leader Kim Jong Un signed a strategic partnership deal which in part focused on expanding military cooperation. That meant large-scale weapons shipments as well as the deployment of North Korean soldiers to support Russia's war in Ukraine. At the same time, both governments agreed to build the new road bridge.

"The opening of the new bridge will boost bilateral trade, optimize logistics, strengthen cultural ties and transform border regions into dynamically growing economic centers," Russian Transport Minister Andrey Nikitin said at the time.

The Washington-based Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS) has also pointed to the bridge's economic significance, noting that "the pace at which construction of the road bridge is progressing, and the continued high level of rail traffic at previously dormant rail yards, are clear indicators of the importance and expansion of trade between the two countries during Russia's ongoing war against Ukraine."

title.en: As Australia is hit with mass mortalities, here’s how NZ has prepared for bird flu
title.zh: 澳大利亚遭遇大规模死亡，新西兰如何为禽流感做准备

summary.en: Australia is experiencing significant wildlife deaths due to bird flu. Its neighbor, New Zealand, has spent years researching how the lethal virus could affect its unique animal populations and preparing for such an event.
summary.zh: 澳大利亚正遭受禽流感导致的野生动物大规模死亡。其邻国新西兰已花费数年时间研究这种致命病毒将如何影响其独特的野生动物，并为此类事件做好了准备。

body.en:
When a swamp harrier hawk — known also as a kāhu — was found tangled in a fence in a thinly populated part of New Zealand's North Island in early July, no one thought much about the discovery.

But when the battered scavenger was put down the following day after its health deteriorated, a routine test would enshrine the bird in history.

It was the first native New Zealand bird to test positive for the highly virulent, often lethal strain of H5N1 bird flu which had been detected on Australia's mainland for the first time just a month prior.

"There's lots of birds that go between Australia and New Zealand; although there is a sea between us, we're way more connected than we might like to think," says Jemma Geoghegan from the University of Otago.

A month on, the virus is slowly making its way into the region's eco-systems. New Zealand has recorded two cases of the virus but officials there expect that number to start climbing steeply any day now.

Australia, meanwhile, has just recorded its first mass casualty event: 49 dead greater crested terns and 35 sick ones were discovered on rocks off Cape Jaffa, an isolated outcrop on South Australia's rugged limestone coast.

Both countries knew the virus was not far off when it was first detected on Australia's remote sub-Antarctic Heard Island in 2025, leading to mass mortality of elephant seals.

By this time, preparations for the strain — which has ripped through every other continent — were well underway in New Zealand, where for the past two years the country's Department of Conservation has been trialling a vaccination program for six species of "highly" endangered birds.

Two years ago the country began researching how certain native birds would tolerate and respond to the vaccine, so when the disease made its inevitable landfall, these populations could be protected.

"The trial was really to understand if the vaccine was going to be effective, but also what kind of doses different birds might need."

She said this "targeted program" had been rolled out for species that were "really, really endangered" and already "highly managed" through GPS trackers and health monitoring.

The vaccine being used in New Zealand requires a booster shot to be effective, so it's important that researchers are able to carefully track which birds have had the jab and which haven't.

"Often they'll be on offshore islands that are highly managed, because there's only maybe a few 100 left of the individuals."

title.en: 'Deeply saddened': Australian helicopter provider speaks after Greece firefighting tragedy
title.zh: “深感悲痛”：希腊消防悲剧后，澳大利亚直升机供应商发声

summary.en: McDermott Aviation, an Australian helicopter provider, has expressed profound sadness following a firefighting tragedy in Greece, where helicopters leased by the company were involved as wildfires continue to spread across southern Europe.
summary.zh: 澳大利亚直升机供应商麦克德莫特航空对希腊消防悲剧表示深切哀悼，该公司租赁的直升机参与了扑灭南欧持续蔓延的野火。

body.en:
Two crew members have died after two helicopters — leased by Australian company McDermott Aviation — collided midair while battling wildfires in Greece on Sunday.

A Greek and a Danish national were killed in the crash over Psatha, an area west of Athens, according to Greece's fire service. Two crew members from Greece and Britain who were operating a separate helicopter were found alive.

Founder and president of McDermott Aviation, John McDermott said he was "deeply saddened" by news of the fatal collision.

"We are deeply saddened to confirm that the two crew members aboard one of the helicopters have lost their lives. The two crew members from the second helicopter are in the care of medical professionals.

"Our thoughts and deepest condolences are with the families, friends and colleagues of those affected by this tragic incident. Both crews were undertaking the critical work of supporting firefighting operations to help protect communities."

McDermott Aviation has reportedly operated in Greece for several years. The company said it is working closely with relevant authorities as they undertake an investigation into the cause of the incident.

Over the past decade, McDermott Aviation said it has engaged in around 10 to 12 international movements a year via sea and air freight. It also operates in New Caledonia, Papua New Guinea, Indonesia and the United States, which is currently experiencing wildfires in several western states.

Nikos Pagiotelis has been a volunteer firefighter in Greece for more than 20 years. He told SBS Greek about the moment he heard news of the crash over local radio.

"When you are inside the fire, and you are trying to help the people, you're trying to save the animals, save the forest. Then suddenly [you] hear that two helicopters have crashed a couple of miles near you — you can understand that something really hurts inside," Pagiotelis said.

"You can do nothing, you freeze for a little bit, and then you just continue your work. You continue to help people to honour the lives of the loss of two comrades."

In a statement on social media, Greek prime minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis also expressed his "sorrow for the tragic accident" and extended condolences to the families of the deceased firefighters.

"The loss of the Greek coordinator and the Danish pilot at the time they were attempting the major fire in Porto Gremeno fills us all with grief," Mitsotakis said.

Nearly 500 firefighters and 23 aircraft have been deployed to fight fires in Greece, which have been driven by high temperatures and gale-force winds.

title.en: Israel kills 18 in Gaza despite Trump's announcement of Hamas disarmament deal
title.zh: 以色列袭击加沙致18人死亡，部长称无协议停止攻击

summary.en: Israeli airstrikes in Gaza have resulted in 18 deaths, continuing despite a US announcement of a potential path for Hamas' disarmament. A minister stated there is no agreement to halt the attacks.
summary.zh: 尽管美国宣布了哈马斯解除武装的途径，以色列对加沙的空袭仍在继续，造成18人死亡。一位部长表示，目前没有停止袭击的协议。

body.en:
Israeli airstrikes hit Gaza for a second straight day on Monday, killing at least 18 Palestinians, medics said, despite US President Donald Trump's announcement of a breakthrough in efforts to implement last year's ceasefire agreement.

From dawn, Israeli warplanes hit Gaza City in the north, the central city of Deir al-Balah and the southern area of Khan Younis, causing the biggest daily death toll in weeks, according to Palestinian health officials.

Trump's assertion on Friday that Hamas and other Palestinian armed groups had agreed to disarm had raised hopes of a turning point in efforts to end the conflict.

On Sunday, Israeli energy minister Eli Cohen — a member of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's security cabinet — said the government would give Hamas the opportunity to disarm but that he was "very sceptical" that would happen.

Cohen told Israel's Army Radio there had been no deal to halt attacks on Gaza and that he saw a need for Israel, which already occupies 70 per cent of the enclave, to take full control of it if Hamas did not disarm.

"In the deal we signed with the United States, our stance is that Hamas must be dismantled. This is the first thing that must happen," he added.

Later on Sunday, a spokesperson for Netanyahu's office told Reuters news agency that Israel expressed concerns to the US on the disarmament plan.

"The most important concern for Israel is that nothing can happen before Hamas completely and truly disarms ...," Doron Spielman, a spokesperson for the Israeli prime minister's office, said.

Strikes on Deir al-Balah killed at least four people, Palestinian health officials said, and a separate attack wounded five people and set some tents ablaze in Mawasi, near Khan Younis, according to the civil emergency service.

A couple and their nine-year-old son were killed in a strike on a house in Mawasi, Palestinian officials said.

Another couple was killed with their child in a strike on an apartment in Gaza City, where two more people died in a strike on a tent near the office of the Egyptian representative mission, medics said. Later on Sunday, another two people were killed in the city's eastern Zeitoun neighbourhood, they added.

One person was killed near Jabalia in northern Gaza, Palestinian officials said.

In a subsequent attack on Gaza City, medics said an Israeli airstrike on a car killed at least three Palestinians near Saraya Square.

Trump's Board of Peace, the US-led body overseeing the ceasefire, published on Friday a 15-point roadmap setting out the final steps for implementing the agreement .

body.zh: 医务人员表示，尽管美国总统唐纳德·特朗普宣布在执行去年停火协议方面取得了突破，但以色列周一连续第二天对加沙进行空袭，造成至少 18 名巴勒斯坦人死亡。 巴勒斯坦卫生官员称，以色列战机从黎明起袭击了北部的加沙城、中部城市代尔巴拉赫和南部的汗尤尼斯地区，造成数周以来单日死亡人数最多的一次。 特朗普周五声称巴勒斯坦哈马斯武装分子和其他武装组织已同意解除武装，这给结束冲突的努力带来了转折点的希望。 周日，以色列能源部长埃里·科恩（总理内塔尼亚胡安全内阁成员）表示，政府将给哈马斯解除武装的机会，但他“非常怀疑”这种情况是否会发生。 科恩告诉以色列陆军电台，目前还没有达成停止对加沙袭击的协议，他认为，如果哈马斯不解除武装，已经控制了该飞地 70% 的以色列需要完全控制该地区。 您值得信赖的来源，让您了解周围世界的最新动态。直接将免费的每日新闻更新和分析发送到您的收件箱。 “在我们与美国签署的协议中，我们的立场是必须解散哈马斯。这是必须发生的第一件事，”他补充道。 周日晚些时候，内塔尼亚胡办公室发言人告诉路透社，以色列向美国表达了对该裁军计划的担忧。 以色列总理办公室发言人多伦·斯皮尔曼说：“以色列最关心的是，在哈马斯完全、真正解除武装之前，什么都不会发生……”。 据民事紧急服务部门称，巴勒斯坦卫生官员称，对代尔巴拉赫的袭击造成至少四人死亡，另一次袭击造成五人受伤，并导致汗尤尼斯附近马瓦西的一些帐篷着火。 巴勒斯坦官员称，一对夫妇和他们 9 岁的儿子在马瓦西一所房屋遭到袭击时丧生。 医务人员称，加沙城一间公寓遭到袭击，另一对夫妇和他们的孩子一起被杀，埃及代表使团办公室附近的帐篷遭到袭击，另有两人死亡。他们补充说，周日晚些时候，又有两人在该市东部的 Zeitoun 街区被杀。 巴勒斯坦官员称，加沙北部贾巴利亚附近有一人被杀。 以色列军方表示，对代尔巴拉赫一间公寓的袭击目标是哈马斯精锐“努赫巴”部队的两名指挥官。 声明补充说，加沙城和贾巴利亚的袭击也针对“军事人员”，但军方仍在审查局势。 在随后对加沙城的袭击中，医务人员表示，以色列对一辆汽车的空袭造成至少三人死亡……

reflection.en: In the face of ongoing conflict and the tragic loss of life, our hearts long for an end to violence. Psalm 46:9 reminds us of Yahweh's ultimate power to make wars cease and break the instruments of conflict. Even amidst persistent strife, this verse offers a vision of a future where true peace prevails.
reflection.zh: 面对持续的冲突和生命的悲剧性逝去，我们的心渴望暴力止息。诗篇46:9提醒我们，雅伟拥有使战争止息、折断争战器械的最终能力。即使在持续的冲突中，这节经文也为我们描绘了一个真正和平终将降临的未来。

verse.textEn: He makes wars cease to the ends of the earth; he breaks the bow and shatters the spear.
verse.textZh: 他止息刀兵，直到地极；他折弓断枪。

title.en: China: Dozens dead in Gansu flash floods

summary.en: Chinese authorities will launch an investigation into the floods, amid warnings of further landslides as the rainy weather continues, after dozens were killed in Gansu province.

body.en:
Chinese authorities will launch an investigation into the floods, amid warnings of further landslides as the rainy weather continues.

The death toll after a flash flood in the northern Gansu province of  China has climbed to 25, according to state media reports.

The flood has left 23 others injured, the ⁠official Xinhua news agency reported on Sunday.

The Shuangshimen Scenic Area, a popular tourist spot for camping, was hit by a flash flood on July 26, with state media initially reporting 10 deaths and 23 injuries.

The country's national commission for disaster prevention said it would oversee an investigation into the event.

Videos of the flood show a deluge ripping through a valley where several tents and cars were parked.

Authorities have warned of further landslides, including in ‌Dingxi, ​as heavy downpour continues in the annual flood season.

Beijing and Inner Mongolia also issued weather warnings on Sunday as China's ​weather observatory warned of heavy rain, high winds and thunderstorms across a large stretch of the country from ⁠the southwest ​to the northeast.

title.en: From petitions to memes: How students made dissent visible
title.zh: 从请愿到网络迷因：学生如何让异议显现

summary.en: Student movements throughout history, from imperial China to modern India, have consistently found new ways to express dissent and challenge established authority, adapting their methods to contemporary tools and symbols.
summary.zh: 从中国古代到当今印度，学生运动不断调整其工具和象征，以挑战权威，使异议得以显现。

body.en:
From imperial China to present-day India, student movements have repeatedly adapted the tools and symbols of their age to challenge authority.

On July 22, 2026, in rainy Mumbai, India , a casually dressed young woman stepped in front of a slow-moving police van carrying detained students. She placed her palm on the hood, forcing the vehicle to stop.

Mobile phones captured the moment from every angle. She too, raised her own phone and recorded the encounter. Within hours, the clip spread across India and beyond.

It became one of the defining visuals of the Cockroach Janta Party protests, a movement in which students demanded transparency and accountability, following leaks in India's medical entrance exams.

But the power of the moment lay not only in what she did, but in how quickly it was seen. A single gesture, a young woman confronting authority , became a symbol shared across millions of screens.

While the clip belongs to a generation raised on social media, the impulse behind it is much older.

From court petitions and revolutionary posters to photographs, umbrellas and memes, student movements have repeatedly adapted the tools and symbols available to them, turning them into vehicles for dissent.

Long before television or social media carried dissent across borders, students still found ways to make their grievances heard.

In Eastern Han China, for instance, scholars at the Imperial Academy (Taixue) aligned with reform-minded officials in opposing powerful eunuchs at court, whom many viewed as corrupt and politically overbearing.

They voiced their objections through public criticism, political networks and petitions.

In an era when political communication moved through official channels, petitions were among the established ways of bringing grievances before the throne. Written in formal language and delivered through the bureaucracy, they carried student concerns directly into the state's communication system.

In Paris in 1968, students challenged university authorities and a conservative postwar social order. As demonstrations spread across the French capital and drew in workers, one of the movement's most enduring contributions emerged from a basement workshop at the Ecole des Beaux-Arts.

The Atelier Populaire ("People's Workshop") printed thousands of posters during the protests, many of them overnight. Their bold graphics, silhouettes and slogans became the visual language of the movement. Produced collectively, many carried no individual author's name, helping transform protest into a shared public voice.

The posters and their messages could appear in dozens of places overnight, giving the protest a wide local visual presence.

Protests also became more impactful when images could be transmitted across borders.

body.zh: 从中华帝国到当今的印度，学生运动不断地采用他们那个时代的工具和符号来挑战权威。 2026 年 7 月 22 日，在多雨的印度孟买，一名穿着休闲的年轻女子走到一辆载着被拘留学生的缓慢行驶的警车前。她将手掌放在引擎盖上，迫使车辆停了下来。 手机从各个角度捕捉了这一时刻。她也举起了自己的手机，记录了这次遭遇。几个小时内，这段视频就传遍了印度及其他地区。 它成为蟑螂简塔党抗议活动的标志性视觉效果之一，在印度医学入学考试泄密后，学生们在这场运动中要求透明度和问责制。 但这一刻的​​力量不仅在于她所做的事情，还在于她的所作所为很快被人们看到。一个年轻女子对抗权威的一个动作，成为了数百万屏幕上共享的符号。 虽然这段视频属于在社交媒体上长大的一代人，但其背后的冲动却要古老得多。 从法庭请愿书和革命海报到照片、雨伞和模因，学生运动不断地调整他们可用的工具和符号，将它们变成异议的工具。 早在电视或社交媒体跨境传播异议之前，学生们就已经找到了表达不满的方法。 例如，在中国东汉，太学的学者与具有改革思想的官员结盟，反对宫廷中有权有势的宦官，许多人认为宦官腐败且在政治上专横。 他们通过公开批评、政治网络和请愿来表达他们的反对意见。 在政治沟通通过官方渠道进行的时代，请愿是向王室表达不满的既定方式之一。它们以正式语言编写并通过官僚机构传达，将学生的担忧直接传达到国家的沟通系统中。 1968 年的巴黎，学生们挑战大学当局和保守的战后社会秩序。随着示威活动在法国首都蔓延并吸引了工人，该运动最持久的贡献之一来自巴黎美术学院的一个地下室工作室。 Atelier Populaire（“人民工作室”）在抗议期间印制了数千张海报，其中许多是在一夜之间印制的。他们大胆的图形、轮廓和口号成为了这场运动的视觉语言。许多作品都是集体制作的，没有作者的名字，这有助于将抗议转变为公众的共同声音。 这些海报及其信息可能会在一夜之间出现在数十个地方，使抗议活动在当地得到广泛的关注。 当图像可以跨境传输时，抗议的影响力也变得更大。 在...

title.en: US-China AI rivalry heats up as Chinese models gain ground
title.zh: 中美人工智能竞争加剧，中国模型迎头赶上

summary.en: China's AI platforms are rapidly advancing, narrowing the gap with US technology. This progress has led to renewed threats from the Trump administration, alongside accusations of intellectual property theft, raising concerns about escalating tensions between the two nations.
summary.zh: 中国的人工智能平台正迅速缩小与美国同行的差距。这一进展引发了特朗普政府新的威胁，并伴随着知识产权盗窃的指控，令人担忧两国之间的紧张关系可能升级。

body.en:
China's AI platforms are rapidly closing the gap with their US counterparts, prompting fresh threats from the Trump administration. With accusations of intellectual property theft, could tensions boil over?

In what seems like the blink of an eye,  China has gone from being up to five years behind the United States in top-tier artificial intelligence (AI) to lagging by just a few months.

While US players, including Anthropic's Claude and OpenAI's ChatGPT , have spent hundreds of billions of dollars to push the frontier of AI, China has pursued a very different path .

Faced with US curbs on high-end chips that help AI to do its most advanced thinking, Chinese tech firms have prioritized dozens of open-source AI models built on "good enough"  technology .

These platforms, including DeepSeek, Alibaba's Qwen and Xiaomi's MiMo, are now widely deployed across Chinese businesses, government services and consumer devices.

In the latest sign of the gap closing, Chinese startup Moonshot AI last week unveiled Kimi K3, a model that rivals one of the most advanced AI models — Anthropic's Claude Fable 5 — on key benchmarks.

In some tests, Kimi K3 matches or even surpasses Claude with far less computing power and at a fraction of the cost. 

Global technology specialist Alvin W. Graylin thinks Kimi K3's arrival turns high-end AI from an expensive luxury into something practical and affordable.

"For 98% of customers, the 1 to 2% difference [in knowledge] isn't worth paying 10 to 20 times more."

China's latest advance has already drawn a strong reaction from Washington, with US President Donald Trump now threatening to block US access to Chinese AI models.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, meanwhile, warned earlier this week that the US could sanction Chinese models over alleged intellectual property (IP) theft.

Anthropic  and OpenAI have accused Chinese labs of using their models to train their own systems, a process known as distilling.

While distilling is a common practice by AI labs worldwide to a limited extent, the companies say their models have been bombarded with queries to harvest advanced reasoning. The White House warned in April that China was doing it on an "industrial scale."

Beijing has hit back, rejecting the accusations as baseless and calling US threats of sanctions and model bans "technological bullying" to contain China's rise.

Giulia Neaher, a research analyst at the Strategic Foresight Hub at the Washington-based Stimson Center think tank, downplayed the role of distilling in Kimi's progress.

body.zh: 中国的人工智能平台正在迅速缩小与美国同行的差距，引发了特朗普政府的新威胁。随着知识产权盗窃的指控，紧张局势会升级吗？ 似乎一眨眼的功夫，中国在顶级人工智能 (AI) 领域就从落后美国五年变为仅落后几个月。 尽管包括 Anthropic 的 Claude 和 OpenAI 的 ChatGPT 在内的美国企业已经花费了数千亿美元来推动人工智能的前沿发展，但中国却走了一条截然不同的道路。 面对美国对帮助人工智能实现最先进思维的高端芯片的限制，中国科技公司优先考虑了数十种基于“足够好”技术的开源人工智能模型。 这些平台，包括 DeepSeek、阿里巴巴的 Qwen 和小米的 MiMo，现已广泛部署在中国企业、政府服务和消费设备中。 作为缩小差距的最新迹象，中国初创公司 Moonshot AI 上周推出了 Kimi K3，该模型在关键基准测试上可与最先进的人工智能模型之一——Anthropic 的 Claude Fable 5 相媲美。 在某些测试中，Kimi K3 可以与 Claude 相媲美甚至超过 Claude，但其计算能力却要低得多，而成本却只是 Claude 的一小部分。 全球技术专家 Alvin W. Graylin 认为 Kimi K3 的到来将高端人工智能从昂贵的奢侈品变成了实用且负担得起的东西。 “对于 98% 的客户来说，[知识] 1% 到 2% 的差异并不值得多付 10 到 20 倍的费用。” 中国的最新进展已经引起华盛顿的强烈反应，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普现在威胁要阻止美国使用中国的人工智能模型。 与此同时，财政部长斯科特·贝森特本周早些时候警告称，美国可能会因涉嫌盗窃知识产权而制裁中国模型。 Anthropic 和 OpenAI 指责中国实验室使用他们的模型来训练他们自己的系统，这一过程被称为蒸馏。 虽然提炼是全球人工智能实验室在一定程度上的常见做法，但这些公司表示，他们的模型已经受到查询的轰炸，以收获高级推理。白宫四月份警告说，中国正在以“工业规模”这样做。 北京方面予以反击，否认这些指控毫无根据，并称美国威胁实施制裁和示范禁令是“技术欺凌”，旨在遏制中国的崛起。 华盛顿智库史汀生中心战略远见中心的研究分析师朱莉娅·尼赫（Giulia Neaher）淡化了提炼在基米进步中的作用。 “[其成功]很大程度上归功于为建设这个项目而投入的人才、基础设施和资源......

summary.en: Home ownership influences how Australians cast their vote, a new study finds.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The ongoing housing crisis is having severe repercussions on individuals and families in Australia. It has limited young people’s ability to move out, increased the rate of involuntary lifelong renting, and pushed vulnerable populations into homelessness.

These are not the only changes that flow as a result of housing unaffordability. Our new research demonstrates it’s also reshaping how people vote.

A longstanding body of academic work links individuals’ assets to their political and ideological beliefs, including the parties they vote for.

This literature shows people with more valuable assets are more likely to hold right-leaning political beliefs. They are also more likely to support conservative parties that favour the status quo over efforts to redistribute money and wealth more equitably throughout a society.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

For the average person, the family home is the most valuable asset they will ever own. However, surprisingly few studies have considered the influence of home ownership on voting preferences. Australia represents an interesting case study for two key reasons.

First, Australian major political parties differ in their electoral positions regarding housing policy. In particular, the Coalition of the Liberal and National parties has historically favoured homeowners through — for example — negative gearing and tax discounts. In contrast, since the 2010s, the Australian Greens and the Labor Party have progressively adopted more pro-renter stances.

Second, Australia’s trend towards housing unaffordability is particularly pronounced by international standards. This is reflected in increased home and rental prices, reduced homeownership rates and increased property-ownership concentration. This situation creates a greater divide in the economic interests of renters and homeowners, potentially shifting (or entrenching) party preferences.

Our new study explored how housing tenure relates to voting behaviour in Australia. We also wanted to know whether the relationship has become stronger over time.

We analysed survey data from more than 19,000 people participating in ten iterations of the Australian Election Study between 1996 and 2022. The Australian Electoral Study interviews people shortly after each national election, collecting information on their demographic traits, economic position and sociopolitical attitudes.

We analysed these survey data to examine associations between individuals’ self-reported housing tenure and the party they voted for in the last election. We also kept other relevant factors constant, such as age, income, area of residence...

summary.en: New international research is challenging fears about a link between children's screen time and developmental delay.

body.en:
Concerns about children and screen use may be overblown, new research suggests, with experts saying worries about an 'iPad baby' generation may be "premature".

A new international study, based on data from over 3,000 children, found no link between screen use duration and developmental difficulties at ages five or 10.

Researchers in the UK spoke with the families of children back in 2009 and 2010 and followed their development for the subsequent 10 years.

Over that time, there has been some criticism and debate about the role of technology in parenting, and whether young people born in the 21st century will be a screen-addicted generation.

The iPad was released in Australia in 2010, and a child growing up around this time is sometimes referred to as an 'iPad baby'.

While the findings are limited by self-reported survey data, Australian experts say the results counter popular messaging about parenting and technology.

"Fear from parents around screen time is unfounded and premature," Associate Professor David Armstrong from the School of Education at La Trobe University told SBS News.

"It's really a mixed bag over whether there are any adverse effects on kids' development, and it's good to note that there are some advantages of devices for social development."

He described the findings as "robust and methodical", saying they contribute to an emerging body of research calling not for less screen time, but for better use of it.

But Professor Andrew Whitehouse, an autism researcher at The Kids Research Institute Australia, said the findings should be taken with a grain of salt, as young children in 2026 have access to more smart devices than in 2009.

"The saturation of childhood by these devices came in the years afterwards," he said in a statement.

"This means that across early childhood, the children had almost no exposure to the ubiquity of smart devices as now exists."

As content increasingly targets children and is designed to maximise viewing time, experts say the best tools parents have are managing content and ensuring quality time away from screens.

Screen time is not inherently harmful said Adam Guastella, a clinical psychologist who works with Sydney Children's Hospital at Westmead and the University of Sydney.

Rather, the effects on a child's physical, cognitive and social development come down to content.

summary.en: Experts warn Australia could face greater competition for key firefighting equipment as officials acknowledge future "challenges".
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
From Spain to Greece, Europe is grappling with unprecedented wildfires that have killed dozens and forced hundreds of thousands of people to evacuate.

Australia is sending help, with two helicopters and dozens of NSW Rural Fire Service (RFS) personnel deploying to France in what is the state service's first-ever firefighting secondment to Europe.

But as Australia sends firefighters and aircraft north, the country's own bushfire season is approaching, which could be worsened by a strengthening El Niño.

For decades, Australia has benefited from a system in which firefighting crews and specialised aircraft can move between the Northern and Southern Hemispheres as fire seasons change.

Climate change is making those seasons longer and increasingly overlap, raising a question that could become increasingly important for Australia: what happens when everyone needs the same aircraft at the same time?

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

The exchange of firefighting crews and aircraft between hemispheres is nothing new.

The RFS has been sending firefighters to North America for decades, with Canada and the United States returning the favour during Australia's summers.

Trent Penman, who leads the FLARE Wildfire Research group at the University of Melbourne, said Australia risks competing for aerial firefighting assets as the Northern and Southern Hemisphere fire seasons increasingly overlap.

"It's a risk that's already been realised both here in Australia and also in North America," he told SBS News.

He pointed to the southern California fires in January last year, which killed 30 people and destroyed 16,000 structures during the height of Australia's summer.

The bushfire season has traditionally followed a relatively predictable pattern, with early-season blazes in southern Queensland, while southern NSW and Victoria experienced fires later in the season.

"Now we're seeing fires starting earlier, but starting earlier in different areas as well," he said.

"We rely very heavily on volunteers in Australia, and so it is really stretching the capacity of our resources."

John Boag, CEO of Avincis, Europe's largest aerial emergency services firm, warned Europe is not prepared for longer and more extreme wildfire seasons, with firefighting aircraft increasingly needed almost year-round.

"Globally, fire seasons are getting longer, aircraft are not moving between areas and pilots are becoming harder and harder to get," Boag told Reuters.

That creates a potential problem for countries such as Australia, which have historically benefited from being able to draw on the same pool of specialised aircraft at different times of the year.

title.en: 'Steadfast advocate': Arnhem Land's Rirratjingu clan elder Bakamumu Marika dies
title.zh: “坚定的倡导者”：阿纳姆地Rirratjingu部落长老巴卡穆穆·马里卡去世

summary.en: Bakamumu Marika, a Rirratjingu clan elder from Arnhem Land, has passed away. He was known for his lifelong dedication to fighting for land rights and championing Indigenous people.
summary.zh: 阿纳姆地Rirratjingu部落长老巴卡穆穆·马里卡去世。他一生致力于为土地权利和原住民争取权益。

body.en:
A respected elder of Arnhem Land's Rirratjingu clan, Bakamumu Marika AM, has died, the clan group's Aboriginal corporation has announced.

"It is with profound sadness that we announce the passing of Bakamumu Marika AM, a highly respected Traditional Owner, elder and senior leader of the Rirratjingu Clan," the statement said.

Marika was a founder, long-serving chairman and current patron of the Rirratjingu Aboriginal Corporation who was appointed a Member of the Order of Australia (AM) in 2022 for his significant community service to North-East Arnhem Land.

As a "steadfast advocate" for land rights, Marika continued one of the most significant legacies in Australia’s Indigenous rights history, honouring and advancing the work of his forefathers, the statement reads.

A proud Rirratjingu man, cultural custodian and champion for his people, Marika dedicated his life to advancing opportunities in education, community development, economic participation and cultural preservation.

His commitment to working collectively, guided by Yolŋu values and traditions, strengthened his community and inspired younger generations to take pride in their culture and identity.

"We honour Bakamumu Marika's legacy and will forever be guided by his own words: 'We must continue to strive for a foundation that provides opportunity for our people. You will carry that responsibility along with my wish that unity and love continue to be the mark of the Rirratjingu people. I say to you, as my father said to me — ‘stand strong like the rock, Mandula'."

The Yothu Yindi Foundation (YYF), host of the Garma Festival , also expressed condolences following Marika's passing.

"Mr Marika was a beloved Yolŋu leader who devoted his life to his family and his people.

"His father, Roy Dadaynga Marika, is regarded as a founder of land rights, a legacy that he continued.

"As the founder and long-serving chairman of the Rirratjiŋu Aboriginal Corporation, he advocated tirelessly for his clan and all Yolŋu."

title.en: Two people seriously injured as building collapses in inner Sydney

summary.en: Two people have been transported to hospital in serious condition after a building collapsed in inner Sydney.

body.en:
Two people have been hospitalised after a building collapsed in central Sydney on Monday, emergency services said.

A spokesperson for New South Wales Ambulance said it was called to an address in Ultimo, a suburb around 2 km from the city's central business district, just before 11am.

Workers assessed seven patients at the scene. According to ABC News, one man in his 60s and another in his 30s were removed from the rubble and rushed to hospital in a serious condition.

One of the men was taken to St Vincent's Hospital Sydney. The other was taken to Royal Prince Alfred Hospital.

Fire and Rescue New South Wales (FRNSW) told ABC News that the building was a construction site. Nearby buildings, including an adjoining service station, have been evacuated.
